findings.title: Keyless Bearer requests reopen the vault on every attempt Priority: Medium
findings.label: bug
findings.body:
## Summary

A deliberately keyless Bearer account still takes the vault-refresh path on every attempt. `account_credential` computes that the account is allowed to run without a credential, but calls `stored_credential` before applying that result. The compiled account carries the conventional fallback secret reference; when that slot is empty, `stored_credential` calls `Vault::refreshed()`, which reopens and reparses the vault.

## Impact

A valid local/keyless Bearer provider performs synchronous filesystem reads and vault parsing on the relay request path for every request. This is a repeatable hot path for an intentionally empty slot and can block a Tokio worker, adding avoidable latency.

## Evidence

- [The missing-slot lookup refreshes the vault](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L2849-L2873).
- [The fallback slot identifies a deliberately keyless account](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L2912-L2915).
- [Credential resolution performs the lookup before returning the keyless state](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L2922-L2950).
- [Vault refresh calls `Self::open` on the same directory](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-core/src/secret.rs#L224-L230).

## Reproduction/verification

Configure a Bearer provider account without an account-owned secret, then send repeated requests. The compiler supplies the conventional fallback slot; the slot is absent; `stored_credential` sees `Ok(None)` and calls `refreshed()` before `account_credential` returns `credential: None`. This is a static call-path verification; no production filesystem tracing or provider call was performed.

## Expected behavior

A known intentionally empty Bearer slot should not reopen the vault on every attempt. Credentials added while the relay is running must remain discoverable through an explicit invalidation or bounded refresh policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Avoid repeated synchronous vault opens for a keyless account whose fallback slot is known to be empty.
- Preserve the ability to observe a credential added after startup through a documented invalidation, file-version, or bounded-refresh mechanism.
- Keep a missing explicitly-owned secret distinct from a deliberately keyless account.
- Continue to fail closed on vault read/decryption errors.

## Regression tests

- Instrument the vault loader and assert repeated keyless requests do not reopen it on every attempt.
- Verify a credential added after startup becomes visible through the selected invalidation/refresh mechanism.
- Keep tests for keyless Bearer accounts and explicitly-owned empty secret slots passing.

findings.title: Combo affinity toggle is mislabeled and has no runtime effect Priority: Low
findings.label: bug
findings.body:
## Summary

The Combo editor labels a toggle “Merge identical consecutive messages when translating between dialects”, but the control reads and writes `draft.affinity`. The model defines `Combo.affinity` as whether the relay keeps the winning step sticky for a conversation. The field is copied into the snapshot, but the relay's sticky predicate does not read it.

## Impact

Operators can save a visible setting that has no runtime effect and believe they enabled message merging or session affinity. This is an inaccurate UI-to-schema contract and an accepted-but-ignored configuration field.

## Evidence

- [Misleading toggle label](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/panel/view-combos.js#L1048-L1050).
- [The editor serializes the toggle as `affinity`](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/panel/view-combos.js#L1110).
- [The model describes affinity as keeping the winning step sticky](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-core/src/model.rs#L1405-L1407).
- [The snapshot carries the field](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-core/src/snapshot.rs#L310) and [copies it from the config](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-core/src/snapshot.rs#L918).
- [Runtime stickiness checks only strategy and the sticky-success window](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L4499-L4505); it does not consult `combo.affinity`.

## Reproduction/verification

Open a combo in the panel, toggle the control, and save. The request payload changes `affinity`; the relay's `sticky_applies` predicate remains unchanged because it only tests strategy and `sticky_success_window_secs`. This is a static UI-to-model-to-snapshot-to-runtime trace; no browser session was run.

## Expected behavior

Every visible setting must accurately describe the property it edits and have a runtime effect. Either implement session affinity as a real runtime switch and label it accordingly, or remove/disable the unused field. Message merging must not be implied by a field that controls a different concept.

## Acceptance criteria

- Wire `ComboPlan.affinity` into the intended runtime decision, or remove the field from the schema and UI.
- If retained, rename the control to an accurate session-affinity label.
- If message merging is desired, define a separate schema property and implement its translation behavior.

## Regression tests

- Add a panel test asserting the accessible label matches the serialized property.
- Add a config/snapshot/relay contract test proving toggling the field changes the intended runtime behavior.
- If the field is removed, assert the panel no longer serializes it.

findings.title: README still calls bounded same-step account retry unimplemented Priority: Low
findings.label: documentation
findings.body:
## Summary

The README Status section still lists “per-account retry inside a single request” as a known gap, but the relay has a bounded same-step account-retry loop.

## Impact

The project status is misleading for operators evaluating multi-account fallback. It understates behavior that is present in the request path and disagrees with the implementation.

## Evidence

- [README status claim](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/README.md#L279).
- [Retry budget](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L2370-L2376) bounds same-step retries by sibling-account count, capped at eight.
- [Retry condition and repeated attempt](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L2384-L2400) retry only for a retryable account failure while another account remains live.

## Reproduction/verification

Static tracing of `dispatch_routed` confirms that retryable account failures cool the account, re-resolve candidates for the same step, and retry within a bounded loop before falling through to the next step. This is not a retry for malformed requests or every upstream status. No local test binary was available.

## Expected behavior

The README should describe bounded same-step retry and its eligibility conditions rather than saying the feature is absent.

## Acceptance criteria

- Update the README Status section to describe same-step retry for retryable account failures.
- State the current eight-retry cap and the exclusions (for example, malformed-request failures).
- Keep the implementation-status summary aligned with the README.

## Regression tests

- Keep relay tests for same-step account retry and failure exclusions passing.
- Include a test proving a retryable failure on one account can be served by a sibling account.

findings.title: mr config exposes five subcommands that always fail Priority: Low
findings.label: Code not implemented
findings.body:
## Summary

The CLI registers `mr config path|validate|show|edit|set-port`, but every variant reaches a stub that ignores its arguments and returns the same `CliError::failure`.

## Impact

The command tree advertises five concrete operations, but none can be used. Operators must edit files manually or use the panel, and automation invoking any of these commands always receives a failure exit status. The incomplete status is disclosed in the CLI reference and `AGENTS.md`; this is a missing implementation rather than a false documentation claim.

## Evidence

- [Command registration](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/main.rs#L95) exposes the config command group.
- [Dispatch](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/main.rs#L267) sends every config invocation to `config::run`.
- [Unconditional stub](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/config.rs#L44-L46) ignores both `cmd` and `ctx` and returns the same failure.
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/user/12-cli-reference.md#L90-L96) lists the commands and states that they return “not implemented yet”.

## Reproduction/verification

Static dispatch trace: parse any config variant → `Command::Config` → `config::run` → unconditional failure. Therefore `mr config path`, `validate`, `show`, `edit`, and `set-port` all fail without performing their advertised operation. No local CLI binary was available, so this is source-level verification.

## Expected behavior

Each registered subcommand should perform its advertised operation using the existing configuration-directory resolution and safe validate/compile/save path. If intentionally deferred, the variants should not be exposed as executable commands.

## Acceptance criteria

- Implement all five subcommands with documented output and exit-code behavior.
- Route mutations through validation and snapshot compilation before writing; failed validation must leave config and snapshot unchanged.
- Invoke editors safely without shell interpolation of editor or path values.
- Alternatively, remove the command group until the operations are implemented.

## Regression tests

- Invoke each subcommand through the binary against a temporary config directory and assert its documented result.
- Assert invalid changes return validation exit 3 and do not modify config or snapshot.
- Assert `--json` emits one valid JSON document for read commands.
- Assert editor failures return a clear error without modifying the file.

findings.title: mr vault list and rekey are registered but always fail Priority: Low
findings.label: Code not implemented
findings.body:
## Summary

The CLI registers `mr vault list` and `mr vault rekey`, but both variants reach a stub that ignores the selected command and returns `CliError::failure`.

## Impact

The CLI advertises vault inspection and key rotation but neither operation is available. Operators cannot use the CLI to list safe secret fingerprints or rotate the vault encryption key. Automation invoking either command always receives a failure exit status. The incomplete status is disclosed in the CLI reference and `AGENTS.md`.

## Evidence

- [Command registration](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/main.rs#L92) exposes the vault command group.
- [Dispatch](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/main.rs#L266) routes every vault invocation to `vault::run`.
- [Unconditional stub](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/vault.rs#L22-L24) ignores the selected variant and returns the same failure.
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/user/12-cli-reference.md#L90-L96) lists both commands and states that they return “not implemented yet”.

## Reproduction/verification

Static dispatch trace: `mr vault list` or `mr vault rekey` → `Command::Vault` → `vault::run` → unconditional failure. Neither command reads the vault or performs the operation. No local CLI binary was available, so this is source-level verification.

## Expected behavior

`list` should enumerate stored secret references and safe fingerprints without printing secret values. `rekey` should rotate the vault encryption key with crash-safe persistence and a fail-closed recovery path. If these operations are deferred, their variants should not be exposed as executable operations.

## Acceptance criteria

- Implement `list` so output contains only IDs, labels, and non-reversible fingerprints.
- Implement `rekey` with an atomic/rollback-safe sequence that cannot leave the vault encrypted under a lost key if a write or rename fails.
- Preserve restrictive file permissions for the vault and key throughout rotation.
- Alternatively, remove the command group until the operations are implemented.

## Regression tests

- Run `mr vault list` against a temporary vault and assert expected fingerprints appear while plaintext credentials do not.
- Run `mr vault rekey` against a temporary vault, verify every stored entry remains decryptable with the new key, and verify the old key no longer decrypts the new vault.
- Inject failures at each persistence/rename step and assert recovery leaves a usable vault/key pair.
- Assert the command never prints credential material to stdout or stderr.

findings.title: Relay never enforces client-key model and route allow-lists Priority: High
findings.label: Code not implemented
findings.body:
## Summary

Client-key `allow_models` and `allow_routes` are accepted by the CLI and panel, persisted in config, copied into the relay's `KeyEntry`, and described by the configuration reference as restrictions. The relay authenticates the presented key hash but never checks those lists before routing. The existing `ClientKey::permits` helper is not called by the relay request path.

## Impact

A caller holding a key configured for a narrow model/route set can still invoke other configured models and registered API routes, provided the key itself is valid. This defeats per-client least-privilege controls and can expose more expensive providers or API surfaces than the operator intended. The API guide explicitly warns that these fields are not enforced, so operators are cautioned, but the configuration reference, CLI flags and panel still present them as restrictions.

## Evidence

- [The model implements `ClientKey::permits`](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-core/src/model.rs#L1770-L1782), but repository code search finds no relay call.
- [Relay `KeyEntry` carries both allow-lists](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/state.rs#L237-L291).
- [Authentication returns the matching entry after hash comparison](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/state.rs#L557-L581).
- [Routed dispatch authenticates but does not call the permission helper](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L1994-L2000); the later quota branch uses the entry for metering, not model/route authorization.
- [The configuration reference says non-empty lists restrict the key](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/03-configuration.md#L425-L436).
- [The API guide warns that the restrictions are not enforced](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/user/03-calling-the-api.md#L109).
- The CLI and panel expose these fields as restrictions in [`key.rs`](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/mr-cli/src/key.rs#L51-L56) and [`view-keys.js`](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/panel/view-keys.js#L172-L218).

## Reproduction/verification

Configure a client key with `allow_models: ["provider/allowed-model"]` and `allow_routes: ["chat.completions"]`. Authenticate a request with that key but name another configured model, or call `/v1/messages`. Static control-flow tracing shows the hash match yields `AuthOutcome::Ok`; the relay accepts `auth.is_allowed()` and proceeds without consulting either list. No live provider was contacted and no local mock was run.

## Expected behavior

Enforce the authenticated key's model and route restrictions before quota admission and before any upstream side effect on every supported relay surface. Empty lists should remain unrestricted; non-empty lists should use the documented exact/glob semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- Enforce `allow_models` against the client-requested model according to documented glob rules.
- Enforce `allow_routes` against the canonical `RouteKind` for every routed endpoint.
- Define and test the policy for `GET /v1/models`, batch and locally served API families so they cannot bypass a restricted key's route policy.
- Refuse a denied request with a stable authorization error before quota reservation or upstream dispatch.
- Keep empty allow-lists unrestricted and preserve existing authentication and quota behavior.
- Align the configuration reference, CLI help, panel hints and API guide with the implemented behavior.

## Regression tests

- With a mock upstream, prove an allowed model/route succeeds and a disallowed model returns an authorization refusal without an upstream call.
- Prove an allowed model on a disallowed route is refused before upstream dispatch.
- Cover OpenAI and Anthropic client routes, Responses, embeddings, audio, image, model listing, batch and local-family surfaces as applicable.
- Test exact names, trailing-star globs, wildcard entries, aliases/combos and empty-list unrestricted behavior.
- Retain tests for missing/invalid key authentication and per-key quota admission.

findings.title: Local batch, eval and vector-store calls bypass client-key quotas Priority: High
findings.label: bug
findings.body:
## Summary

Several authenticated local API families do not preserve the client key's quota context when they make upstream requests. `authorize_batch_request` only authenticates and discards the resulting `AuthOutcome::Ok(KeyEntry)`. The internal dispatch helper then marks nested work `pre_authorized: true` with `pre_admitted: None`; `dispatch_routed` converts that to `AuthOutcome::Open`, and its quota admission branch only reserves a ticket for `AuthOutcome::Ok(entry)`.

This affects batch submission, eval runs and vector-store embedding calls. The separate batch KV budget is not a per-client request/token quota.

## Impact

A valid client key configured with `limit_requests` or rolling request/token caps can use these routes to trigger provider work without consuming its per-key budget. A batch can contain many items; an eval run dispatches model work per item (and can dispatch a grader); vector-store operations dispatch embedding batches. This defeats the operator's per-key spend limits and can create unmetered upstream cost.

## Evidence

- [Batch creation authenticates and then proceeds without client-key quota admission](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/batch.rs#L2559-L2570).
- [Batch module documentation says the submission should be treated as one metered request](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/batch.rs#L106-L110), but the handler only calls the authenticate-only helper.
- [Eval execution dispatches each item internally](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/evals.rs#L540-L565); the grader path also uses `dispatch_internal` at [line 985](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/evals.rs#L985).
- [Vector-store embedding batches use internal dispatch](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/vector_stores.rs#L1863-L1877).
- [Internal dispatch explicitly bypasses client authentication and admission](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L1815-L1844) by setting `pre_authorized: true` and `pre_admitted: None`.
- [The request path maps pre-authorized work to `AuthOutcome::Open`](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L1994-L2000), while [quota admission only handles metered authenticated entries](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L2036-L2055).
- [The shared helper only checks whether authentication succeeded](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/crates/manarouter-relay/src/server.rs#L6473-L6481); it does not reserve or return a quota ticket.
- [The API specification says eval runs are per-request, batches are one metered submission, and local families must apply quota when they make upstream calls](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/30-openai-compatible-api-spec.md#L610-L612) ([local-family rule](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/30-openai-compatible-api-spec.md#L676-L679), [batch metering contract](https://github.com/RobertoTornel/Manarouter/blob/fc8e6a6d2bd9b1f6055907533b6429a28edfa7db/docs/30-openai-compatible-api-spec.md#L863-L865)).

## Reproduction/verification

Configure a client key with `limit_requests: 1` (or a one-request rolling cap), consume the allowance with one ordinary routed request, then submit a batch, run an eval, or trigger vector-store embedding work with the same key. Static tracing shows the local handler authenticates but does not reserve the client's quota, and nested dispatch is treated as open/unmetered. This is source-level verification; no provider, paid account or production quota was contacted.

## Expected behavior

Client-initiated local-family work must retain the authenticated key identity and use the documented quota unit: one admission for a batch submission, per-request admission for eval model calls, and admission for each vector-store embedding call that reaches a provider. Internal dispatch must not silently convert client work into an open request.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve the authenticated `KeyEntry` (or an equivalent admission context) from the local handler into internal dispatch.
- Reserve and settle one client-key quota ticket for a batch submission, not zero and not one per item.
- Apply the documented per-request quota to eval model/grader calls.
- Apply quota to each vector-store embedding batch that invokes an upstream provider.
- Ensure retries/fallbacks inherit the original ticket rather than charging twice.
- Keep the independent batch KV budget and worker limits intact.

## Regression tests

- A key with a one-request cap can submit exactly one batch; a second batch is refused before provider dispatch.
- A batch with multiple items consumes one client-key request admission, as documented.
- Eval runs consume the documented per-request quota and stop before upstream dispatch when exhausted.
- Vector-store embedding work consumes quota and is refused when the key is exhausted.
- Assert unmetered keys still work and internal retries inherit one ticket.
